understanding.purpose: A compact order or fulfillment table showing item details, amounts, warehouse locations and tracking identifiers.
understanding.reading: Readers scan across a row to check an item and its fulfillment details, and down columns to compare quantities, prices and totals.
groups: ID and SKU identify each line item.
Color and Size describe the item variant.
Qty, Price, Tax and Total describe the quantity and monetary amounts.
Warehouse and Tracking describe fulfillment and shipment.
keep_intact: SKU and warehouse codes where space permits
may_wrap: Warehouse locations at hyphens; their wrapping can share row height with wrapped SKUs

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Split the 8px difference between the two designs. Test whether the intermediate allocation produces more balanced SKU and warehouse breaks while retaining the same row height.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Give SKU enough width to aim for two lines per item, reclaiming spare space from the short columns and reducing Warehouse while retaining room for its longest word. Keep tracking and numeric values intact.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Test a more balanced allocation between SKU and Warehouse. It gives SKU substantially more room than r0C while leaving Warehouse more breathing space than the SKU-priority design.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Give Warehouse another 4px from SKU to test whether its location breaks improve. SKU remains wide enough for its individual unbreakable segments.

bad.name: r0C
bad.note: Share space between SKU and warehouse while giving the short descriptive and financial columns a little breathing room.
bad.why: The narrow SKU column breaks two identifiers across three lines, while extra width in several short columns does little to improve scanning.

bad.name: r3A
bad.note: Move 23px from SKU to Warehouse. This tests whether more complete warehouse locations can be shown while SKU codes still wrap cleanly into two lines.
bad.why: All three SKUs occupy three lines, making the identifiers harder to compare and leaving large areas of empty space in the other cells.

bad.name: r3B
bad.note: Give Warehouse its full one-line content width and use the remaining space for SKU. This tests whether intact locations are worth a potentially tighter SKU wrap.
bad.why: Four-line SKUs fragment the identifiers and make every row disproportionately tall just to keep warehouse names on one line.

bad.name: r3C
bad.note: Move 18px from SKU to Warehouse as a moderate alternative, preserving more SKU space while testing for improved warehouse breaks.
bad.why: Two SKUs occupy three lines, producing uneven row heights for the modest benefit of a shorter warehouse wrap.

rationale: r2A gives the SKU and warehouse fields enough room to wrap at hyphens within two lines, while tracking numbers remain intact. The three data rows consequently share a consistent height, and the compact numeric columns remain easy to scan. Its allocation balances the two variable-length descriptive fields without spending width on already short values.

general: Protect unbreakable identifiers and keep related numeric values easy to compare.
Allocate width according to content and reading priority; equal column widths are rarely necessary.
Judge wrapping by its effect on row coherence and legibility, not table height alone.
specific: Tracking needs 180 px to preserve the longest value, including padding and borders.
A modest exchange of width between SKU and Warehouse preserves the same two-line row rhythm.

tradeoffs: A wider warehouse column makes its location codes easier to read, but taking too much space from SKU fragments product identifiers and increases row heights.
uncertain: r1A, r1B, r2A and r2B are close; a designer who prioritizes either SKU or warehouse codes could reasonably choose a different one. The ranges are conservative, based on the supplied renderings: SKU and Warehouse widths must move in opposite directions to preserve the 784 px total.

critique.good: SKU and warehouse locations generally wrap at hyphens, keeping the rows relatively compact.
critique.problems: Size and Qty break across lines; White, several monetary values, and both tracking identifiers split within words or numbers. These breaks make comparison and identification harder.
critique.cause: Size at 51px, Qty at 46px, Color at 60px, Price at 61px, Tax at 52px, Total at 67px, and Tracking at 179px each fall just short of their required content widths.

critique.good: The wide Warehouse column keeps locations on one line.
critique.problems: SKUs stack into as many as four lines, making the table tall and leaving large empty areas in the other columns. Headers, values, and tracking identifiers also split within words or numbers.
critique.cause: Warehouse takes 148px, while SKU receives only 74px. The other undersized columns have the same problems as in r0A.

critique.good: All headers, words, monetary values, and tracking identifiers stay intact. The header row is compact, and warehouse locations wrap at hyphens.
critique.problems: The second and third SKUs need three lines, making those rows taller than the first. Several short columns have a few pixels of spare width that could help the SKU column.
critique.cause: SKU has 89px, while Warehouse has 114px and several short columns exceed their minimum content widths.

critique.good: Headers, numbers and tracking identifiers stay on one line. SKU and warehouse breaks align within the same two-line rows, preserving a consistent row rhythm.
critique.problems: The warehouse locations break into uneven fragments, with the final location leaving a short “01” on its second line. The wide tracking column also dominates the table visually, although its width is needed for the identifiers.
critique.cause: The 103px warehouse column leaves 82px for text, just enough for the longest individual word but not the complete locations. The 180px tracking column is required to accommodate a 159px identifier plus padding and border.

critique.good: The extra warehouse width gives that column a little more breathing room, while headers, numeric values and tracking identifiers remain intact. Rows retain the same consistent two-line height.
critique.problems: The warehouse locations still wrap, and the narrower SKU column does not reduce the table height. Both descriptive fields remain visually fragmented across each row.
critique.cause: Moving 8px from SKU to Warehouse leaves 91px and 90px of text space respectively; neither is wide enough to keep its longest full value on one line.

critique.good: Headers, amounts, and tracking identifiers stay intact. Each item reads across a consistent two-line row, and the SKU and warehouse wraps share that height.
critique.problems: The warehouse wraps all three locations, leaving the final row with a lone “01” on its second line. The SKU column has more room than it needs for its current two-line breaks.
critique.cause: The 107px warehouse width leaves 86px for text; the 116px SKU width leaves 95px.

critique.good: The table keeps the same clear hierarchy and consistent row rhythm as r2A. The SKU still wraps at meaningful hyphens, and tracking and numeric values remain intact.
critique.problems: The extra warehouse width does not visibly improve the breaks: all three locations still wrap, including the isolated “01” in the last row.
critique.cause: At 115px, the warehouse has 94px of text space, still short of the width needed for the longer location strings. The 108px SKU column has room to give up if its existing breaks are preserved.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r0C.why: Tracking and the numeric columns remain intact, but the narrow SKU column forces two identifiers onto three lines and makes the rows uneven.

r1A.why: The identifiers wrap consistently over two lines, tracking stays intact, and the numeric columns are easy to compare. Warehouse values also wrap.

r2A.why: Two-line SKU and warehouse values give the rows a consistent rhythm, while tracking and numeric values remain intact.

ref_equal.why: Equal-width columns waste space on short values while breaking the Warehouse and Tracking headers and splitting tracking numbers into fragments. SKU values also span four lines.

r1B.why: SKU values wrap consistently over two lines, tracking numbers remain intact, and the numeric columns are compact and legible. Warehouse values wrap across two lines.

ref_auto.why: Compact short-value columns leave room for tracking numbers, and all SKUs use two lines. The last warehouse value fits on one line, giving it a slightly different rhythm from the other rows.

raw.unsure: B, C, E and F are close; the preference for F rests on its slightly more generous warehouse column and compact short-value columns.

ref_equal.why: Equal-looking widths waste space in short fields while breaking the Warehouse and Tracking headers and splitting identifiers across several lines.

r0C.why: Tracking stays intact and the numeric fields scan well, but the narrow SKU column creates three-line entries and uneven row heights.

r1A.why: Tracking stays intact, SKU entries fit on two lines, and the numeric fields remain easy to compare. Warehouse values wrap onto two lines.

r1B.why: The columns are well balanced, with intact tracking numbers and consistent two-line SKU and warehouse entries.

ref_auto.why: Tracking numbers stay intact, SKUs use two lines, and the wider warehouse column keeps the Leipzig value on one line. Short numeric columns remain easy to scan.

r2A.why: Tracking numbers stay intact and SKUs fit on two lines, though all warehouse values wrap.

raw.unsure: C, D and F are very similar; their small width differences have little visible effect on readability.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
